newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati testifies in court.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati testifies in court.

text.p: Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri testified in court on Monday for the first time in the trial of 124 party supporters in connection with riots that rocked Jakarta on July 27.

Eyewitnesses in the court quoted her as saying she had been told on July 25 of an impending attack on the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) she had headed before being ousted by a government-backed rebel faction.
She was quoted as saying she had tried unsuccessfully to contact the people she believed were behind the proposed attack to make them call it off.
She said she had never been told by police or anyone else to vacate the PDI headquarters. But she also said she had given no orders to her supporters to defend it.
Those on trial have been accused of assault and disobeying police orders.

Megawati loyalists had occupied the bungalow-style headquarters in central Jakarta to prevent the rebel faction -- now recognised by the government as heading the party -- from taking over the building.
Backers of rebel faction leader Surjadi, the deputy speaker of parliament and a former PDI leader, attacked the building with police support on the morning of July 27.
The raid sparked the riots in one part of the capital in which a number of buildings and vehicles were burned.
Defence laywers for those on trial have complained the police arrested only the defenders of the PDI headquarters, and left the attackers alone.
The official Human Rights Commission said five people died, 149 people were injured and 23 were missing as a result of the riots.
Asked after Monday's hearing how she felt about the court process, she replied: "Good."
"I hope that the outcome will be in line with what we want," she added.
Asked about the people still missing, she said: "The people that may be missing have not returned yet or reported to their families. Maybe they died, but we don't know."
The government has blamed the riots on the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD), a number of whose members have been accused of subversion, which carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
